handback.title: First release v0.1.0 with a changelog
handback.summary: Dokima gets its first version, v0.1.0, with a tag, a GitHub release and a changelog.
handback.user_story: Owners see Dokima as a product with versions: a v0.1.0 release and a changelog saying what it does.

acceptance_criteria.text: When the changelog reaches main, the v0.1.0 tag is made at that commit.
acceptance_criteria.words: A workflow makes the tag and the release when the changelog merges

edge_cases.case: A later push to main, once v0.1.0 exists, makes nothing new.

acceptance_criteria.text: When the changelog reaches main, a GitHub release named v0.1.0 is made.
acceptance_criteria.words: A workflow makes the tag and the release when the changelog merges

edge_cases.case: GitHub refuses the release, so the run fails where the owner sees it.

acceptance_criteria.text: When v0.1.0 is released, its notes are the changelog's v0.1.0 section, nothing more.
acceptance_criteria.words: the release notes are the changelog's v0.1.0 section

edge_cases.case: The changelog also holds an Unreleased section, which stays out of the notes.

raises.label: Changelog needs own issue
raises.text: The owner moved the changelog listing what v0.1.0 does to its own issue. No open issue holds it yet.
raises.evidence: Owner's comment https://github.com/dokima-dev/dokima/issues/755#issuecomment-6244851037; no open issue in open_issues.json names a changelog.

answers.why: The owner settled it: the changelog list is its own issue; this story keeps the tag and release.
